mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly growth in real GDP (GDPC1) above 2.0% annually signals strong economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved corporate earnings outlook.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of quarters where GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annually, or the 20-day return correlation with GDPC1 growth is below 0.15 (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.0% for two consecutive months, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy phase that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% for two consecutive months occurs in more than 60% of cases where the 20-day forward return is positive, or the average 20-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.0% and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 120.0 indicates a deteriorating labor market and supply contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The condition UNRATE>5.0 AND INDPRO<120.0 occurs in more than 40% of cases where the 20-day forward return is positive, or the average 20-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS rising above 3.5% and CPIAUCSL rising above 3.0% annually), the S&P 500 tends to underperform, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and higher inflation expectations.
failure_condition: The condition FEDFUNDS>3.5 AND CPIAUCSL>3.0 occurs in more than 60% of cases where the 60-day forward return is positive, or the average 60-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 115.0 for two consecutive months signals a supply shock that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market volatility and risk-off sentiment.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 115.0 for two consecutive months occurs in more than 50% of cases where the 5-day forward return is positive, or the average 5-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (RSAFS) above 350,000 million dollars signals strong housing market activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to improved consumer confidence and economic growth.
failure_condition: RSAFS > 350,000 million dollars occurs in more than 40% of cases where the 20-day forward return is negative, or the 20-day return correlation with RSAFS is below 0.15 (p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary easing cycle (defined by FEDFUNDS falling below 3.0% and CPIAUCSL below 2.5% annually), the S&P 500 tends to outperform, leading to positive forward returns over the next 60 trading days due to lower discount rates and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: The condition FEDFUNDS<3.0 AND CPIAUCSL<2.5 occurs in more than 60% of cases where the 60-day forward return is negative, or the average 60-day return in triggered periods is not significantly positive (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% and decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) below 133,000 thousand persons indicates a severe labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to recession fears.
failure_condition: The condition UNRATE>5.5 AND PAYEMS<133000 occurs in more than 40% of cases where the 20-day forward return is positive, or the average 20-day return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p>0.05).
